instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment.
Scrub the sweet potatoes and pat them dry. Leave the skin on. Cut each one lengthwise into slices about 1/4 inch thick. You want 8 slices from the widest middle parts.
Arrange the slices on the baking sheet in a single layer. Brush them with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and sprinkle with 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper.
Bake for 8 minutes. Flip the slices and bake for 6 to 8 minutes, until a fork slides in easily and the edges are browned. Don't let them go much longer or they fall apart.
Meanwhile, slice the bananas. In a bowl, mash the avocados with 1/4 tsp salt with a fork.

Heat the last 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Crack in the 4 eggs and cook for 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft. Cook them a little longer if you like the yolks firm.
Spread 4 of the slices with the almond butter and top with the banana.
Spread the other 4 slices with the avocado and top each with a fried egg.
Serve with a fork and knife.
method_notes: The sources agree on thin lengthwise slices of sweet potato cooked until tender and browned, then used like bread. Cozymeal (the lead) bakes slices 1/4 to 1/3 inch thick at 400°F and gives both a sweet topping of almond butter and banana and a savory one of avocado and a fried egg. The Toasted Pinenut fries the slices in ghee instead. This version follows the lead's oven method, with the bake time lengthened a little so the slices are properly tender. Half the slices get the sweet topping and half the savory one. The lead has only 2 ratings, so this is a fallback.
